entities.summary: Robert Ames Bennet (1870–1954) was an American writer of westerns and science fiction. Early in his career Bennet wrote short stories, drama scripts, and novels for a variety of genres under the pen name Lee Robinet. By the 1930s he was primarily a western writer, penning such stories as Caught in the Wild, Go-Getter Gary, and Guns on the Rio Grande. Several of his novels were made into films, including "Finders Keepers" and "Out of the Depths". His Thyra: A Romance of the Polar Pit is considered a classic of the Lost World genre and is listed in 333: A Bibliography of the Science-Fantasy Novel a collection of the best efforts in Science-Fantasy up to and including 1950.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a prolific western and science fiction writer, Robert Ames Bennet's works were adapted into films such as 'Finders Keepers' and 'Out of the Depths', contributing to the popularization of these genres in the early 20th century. His novel 'Thyra: A Romance of the Polar Pit' is considered a classic of the Lost World genre, influencing subsequent authors.
